title: The number of studies the sample was drawn from
published: We compiled a list of [[all 97]] archived studies[[, excluded three books,]] and then randomly selected 20 studies (Peer, Orr, and Coppock 2021).
corrected: We compiled a list of [[92]] archived studies and then randomly selected 20 studies (Peer, Orr, and Coppock 2021).
note: The sentence implies a sampling frame of 94 studies, 97 less 3 books. The study list the sampling script reads, ISPSDataArchive_StudyList_20191108.csv, has 92 rows, and drawing 20 from that list with the seed and sampler the authors used returns exactly the 20 study ids the deposit carries. The list has no field marking a book. The published 97 and 3 books cannot be reconciled with the 92-row list from the deposited or archived materials, so either the total or the exclusion count is misstated, and the corrected sentence states only what the materials show. The sample of 20, its selection, and every count computed from it are unaffected.

title: A percentage printed one point too high in Table 1
note: 8 of 11 studies is 72.7 per cent, which rounds to 73. The neighbouring cell, 3 (27%), is 27.3 per cent and is rounded correctly, and the column's two percentages, 27 and 73, then sum to 100. The count of 8 is right.

title: The Gertler and Bullock reference prints a first page in place of a page range
published: Gertler, Aaron L., and John G. Bullock. 2017. “Reference Rot: An Emerging Threat to Transparency in Political Science.” PS: Political Science & Politics 50 (1): [[166]].
corrected: Gertler, Aaron L., and John G. Bullock. 2017. “Reference Rot: An Emerging Threat to Transparency in Political Science.” PS: Political Science & Politics 50 (1): [[166--71]].
note: Crossref, doi 10.1017/s1049096516002353, gives the article's pages as 166 to 171. The corrected range keeps the reference list's own style, which drops the leading digits a last page shares with the first (Alvarez, Key, and Núñez 2018 prints 422–26).
